# Transient global amnesia

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Neurology > Disorders of consciousness > Transient global amnesia*

[Original Article Link](/library/4R03Mf)

---

## Summary

Transient <u>global amnesia</u> (<u>TGA</u>) is a neurological disorder characterized by acute, transient <u>memory</u> loss lasting ≤ 24 hours. The etiology of <u>TGA</u> is unclear, but certain triggers (e.g., physical exertion, psychological <u>stress</u>) have been identified. Affected individuals experience a sudden inability to retain new information (i.e., <u>anterograde amnesia</u>), with or without partial <u>retrograde amnesia</u>. Patients often present with mild <u>agitation</u>, <u>anxiety</u>, and/or <u>disorientation</u> but are typically alert and oriented to self. No other new neurological deficits or cognitive impairments are present. <u>TGA</u> is a <u>clinical diagnosis</u>, but diagnostic studies (e.g., <u>MRI</u>, <u>laboratory studies</u>, <u>EEG</u>) are often obtained to rule out other causes of <u>amnesia</u>. The condition is <u>self-limited</u> by definition, and no specific treatment is indicated. <u>TGA</u> recurs in a minority of patients, but the prognosis is otherwise good.

---

## Etiology

* <u>Idiopathic</u>  [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)[[3]](/library/ywddlH0)

* Precipitating factors (common) [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)[[3]](/library/ywddlH0)

* Physical exertion (e.g., athletic activity, sexual intercourse, strenuous work)

* Psychological <u>stress</u>

* Medical procedures

* Severe <u>pain</u>

* Extreme temperatures (e.g., sudden immersion in cold water)

---

## Clinical features

* Abrupt onset

* Anterograde <u>amnesia</u> with or without partial <u>retrograde amnesia</u>

* No <u>focal neurological deficits</u> or other new cognitive impairments

* Preserved alertness and orientation to self

* Patients often present with mild <u>agitation</u>, <u>disorientation</u>, and/or <u>anxiety</u>.

* Return to baseline within 24 hours (often within 6 hours)  [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)





> [!WARNING]
> Rapidly recurring episodes of acute <u>amnesia</u> lasting < 1 hour suggest transient <u>epileptic</u> <u>amnesia</u> rather than <u>TGA</u>.[[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)

---

## Diagnosis

### <u>Clinical diagnosis</u> [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)[[3]](/library/ywddlH0)




* <u>TGA</u> is <u>diagnosed clinically</u> based on the typical <u>clinical features of TGA</u>, including:

* Complete resolution within 24 hours

* No changes in the <u>level of consciousness</u>

* No recent <u>head injury</u> or <u>seizures</u>

* Diagnostic studies are not required for <u>TGA</u> but are commonly obtained to rule out differential diagnoses.





> [!TIP]
> Consider <u>TGA</u> in patients with new-onset <u>amnesia</u> lasting ≤ 24 hours and no other neurological findings.




### <u>MRI</u> [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)




* Indication

* Obtain when a structural cause of transient <u>amnesia</u> is suspected.

* Consider within 12–24 hours of symptom onset to support the diagnosis.

* Findings: focal, <u>hyperintense</u> lesions in the <u>hippocampus</u>





> [!WARNING]
> <u>Focal neurological deficits</u> and/or <u>seizures</u> exclude <u>TGA</u>. Obtain <u>CNS</u> imaging if <u>stroke</u> or other structural lesions are suspected.




### Additional diagnostics [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)




Consider other <u>diagnostics for altered mental status</u> (<u>AMS</u>) to rule out alternative <u>causes of AMS</u>, e.g.:




* <u>Laboratory studies</u>: <u>CBC</u>, <u>CMP</u>, <u>TFTs</u>, ethanol level, urine toxicology

* CT head: if recent <u>head injury</u> or <u>hemorrhagic stroke</u> are suspected

* <u>EEG</u>: if there is concern for <u>seizure</u> (e.g., in patients with recurrent episodes of <u>amnesia</u>)

---

## Treatment

<u>TGA</u> is a <u>self-limited</u> condition. No specific treatment is indicated once the differential diagnosis is ruled out. [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)[[4]](/library/-wdDlH0)[[5]](/library/Xca9aj)




* Observe the patient until <u>amnesia</u> has fully resolved.

* Reassure patient and caregivers.

---

## Prognosis

* Resolves spontaneously within 24 hours

* <u>TGA</u> recurs in up to 25% of patients. [[1]](/library/AwdRlH0)
